calls.reason: The claim depends on the boom actually ending, and the packet shows no qualifying end. OpenAI closed a $122B round in March 2026, and the October 2026 Reuters report describes market stress, not a collapse.

Semafor (Jan 2024) reported that some backer money came as cloud credits or contracts, and the FTC found investments had to be largely spent on the backers' clouds. Microsoft and Amazon each invested billions.
The trigger never clearly happened. Microsoft paused some projects in 2025, but it kept its 2026 capex plans unchanged and expected FY27 capex to grow, so the predicted collapse cannot be tested.

Investors did question the spending (Reuters, Feb 2025), but the revenue part is hedged with 'likely'. Microsoft also reported AI services adding 16 points of Azure growth, and no capex total matches the $100bn figure.

No cash records show the minimum OpenAI needed to survive. Its $6.6B round drew on Thrive, Microsoft and Nvidia as well as SoftBank, but was structured as convertible notes, so whether funding stayed in the named channels is unclear.
The customer quoted in contemporary reporting, Heller, expected GPT-5 to be 'better, but not necessarily game-changing'. That doubts a big leap; it is not a clear expectation of no significant jump.
